$comment: Cold tier, and the widest blast radius in the whole configuration: an enabled server is a tool every agent can reach. Nothing is enabled by default. To enable one, move it from `disabled` into `servers` and fill in owner, trust, scope and version. harness doctor refuses an enabled server that is missing any of those, that carries a literal credential, or that still has a TODO in its command, args, owner or version.

cross-tk.$comment: The token-saving server every agent uses first, by rule: once it is declared, the first read of a session goes through it and the crosstk-first hook refuses a built-in read before that. Its launch command is not known to the harness, so this entry is a template: fill in command, args and version from the Cross TK documentation your team uses before moving it into servers. Discovery is by name - the session start reports whether a server matching cross-tk is declared here, and the agents read its real tools from their descriptions at runtime. `tools` lists the tool names as the runtime shows them, only needed when they do not carry the server name; `mandatoryFirst: false` turns the refusal into a one-time reminder.
cross-tk.command: TODO: the Cross TK launch command
cross-tk.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
cross-tk.trust: TODO: state what it reads and writes; a token-saving server usually reads the workspace and returns compact views of it
cross-tk.scope: workspace only, read paths only; anything that writes files or reaches the network needs its own line here
cross-tk.version: pin an exact version before enabling

filesystem.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
filesystem.trust: reads and writes any file under the workspace folder
filesystem.scope: workspace only; a wider root gives every agent read access to the machine
filesystem.version: pin an exact version before enabling

github.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
github.trust: reads issues, pull requests and code for every repository the token can see
github.scope: use a fine-grained token limited to the repositories that need it, read-only unless a workflow genuinely writes
github.version: pin an exact version before enabling

aws.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
aws.trust: acts as the named AWS profile; whatever that role can do, an agent can do
aws.scope: use a read-only role for review work; a role that can apply infrastructure needs the Q4 quadrant and a human at the keyboard
aws.version: pin an exact version before enabling

azure-devops.owner: TODO: the team that answers for this server
azure-devops.trust: reads work items, repositories, pull requests, pipelines and wiki for every project the signed-in identity can see
azure-devops.scope: reading only. Writes go through core/tools/ado/*.mjs, which build the command, support --dry-run and redact secrets. Enabling a write path here would move those actions back into the model territory
azure-devops.version: pin an exact version before enabling
